title: Read From Brain Waves to Words: Brain2Qwerty Offers a New Path to Communication Without Surgery
summary: Brain2Qwerty uses deep learning and a language model to decode typed sentences from non-invasive MEG recordings. In nine healthy volunteers, the best reported mean word-error rate was 0.39; this is offline sentence-decoding research, not a validated communication device or clinical result.
ai_technology: Deep-learning character detection and word-aligned MEG embeddings feed a fine-tuned language model for sentence decoding.

evidence.tested: In nine healthy volunteers, sentence decoding achieved mean word-error rate 0.39 and outperformed encoder-only and encoder-plus-N-gram baselines; an ablation showed MEG-derived tokens contributed.
evidence.unknown: Offline study in healthy volunteers; no patient cohort, low-latency causal decoding, or clinical validation, and fluent incorrect outputs remain possible.
evidence.ai_role: A deep-learning/LLM pipeline decodes typed sentences from non-invasive MEG signals.

source_review.scope: Primary source full-text Methods and Results; version date and reported validation scope checked.
